        "# ─── Standard data handling libraries ───────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "import pandas as pd          # For loading and manipulating tabular data\n",
        "import numpy as np           # For numerical operations and array handling\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Visualization libraries ─────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt   # For creating plots and charts\n",
        "import seaborn as sns             # For prettier statistical visualizations\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Scikit-learn: for preprocessing and evaluation ─────────────────────────\n",
        "from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split   # Split data into train/test\n",
        "from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler       # Normalize numerical features\n",
        "from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder         # Encode text labels to numbers\n",
        "from sklearn.metrics import (confusion_matrix,         # Evaluate model predictions\n",
        "                             classification_report,\n",
        "                             ConfusionMatrixDisplay)\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── TensorFlow / Keras: for building the neural network ─────────────────────\n",
        "import tensorflow as tf\n",
        "from tensorflow import keras\n",
        "from tensorflow.keras import layers\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Suppress unnecessary warnings to keep output clean ──────────────────────\n",
        "import warnings\n",
        "warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')\n",
        "tf.get_logger().setLevel('ERROR')\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Set a random seed so results are reproducible every run ─────────────────\n",
        "np.random.seed(42)\n",
        "tf.random.set_seed(42)\n",
        "\n",
        "print('All libraries imported successfully!')\n",
        "print(f'TensorFlow version: {tf.__version__}')"
      ]
    },

    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "# Task 1: Target Distribution Chart\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── 1f. Distribution of the Target Variable (Visualization) ─────────────────\n",
        "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))\n",
        "\n",
        "# --- Bar chart showing count of churned vs retained customers ---\n",
        "churn_counts = df['churn'].value_counts()\n",
        "axes[0].bar(['Retained (0)', 'Churned (1)'], churn_counts.values,\n",
        "            color=['steelblue', 'tomato'], edgecolor='black')\n",
        "axes[0].set_title('Target Variable Distribution', fontsize=13)\n",
        "axes[0].set_ylabel('Number of Customers')\n",
        "# Add exact numbers on top of each bar\n",
        "for i, v in enumerate(churn_counts.values):\n",
        "    axes[0].text(i, v + 5, str(v), ha='center', fontweight='bold')\n",
        "\n",
        "# --- Pie chart showing percentage split ---\n",
        "axes[1].pie(churn_counts.values,\n",

        "# Task 2: Handle Missing Values\n",

        "    # If there were missing text values, fill them with the most common value\n",
        "    cat_cols = df_clean.select_dtypes(include='object').columns\n",
        "    df_clean[cat_cols] = df_clean[cat_cols].fillna(df_clean[cat_cols].mode().iloc[0])\n",
        "    print('Missing values filled.')"

        "# Task 2: Encode Categorical Columns\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── 2c. Encode Categorical Columns ──────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "# Neural networks only understand numbers, not text like 'North' or 'Premium'.\n",

        "# For example: region 'North' → region_North=1, region_South=0, region_East=0 ...\n",
        "# drop_first=True removes one redundant column per feature to avoid duplication.\n",

        "print(f'\\nNew columns added by encoding:')\n",

        "#  Task 2: Separate Features and Target\n",

        "# Task 2: Train/Test Split\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── 2e. Split into Training and Testing Sets ─────────────────────────────────\n",
        "# We train the model on 80% of the data and test it on the remaining 20%.\n",
        "# This simulates how the model will perform on new, unseen customers.\n",

        "# random_state=42 makes the split reproducible (same split every run).\n",
        "\n",
        "X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(\n",
        "    X, y,\n",
        "    test_size=0.2,       # 20% goes to testing\n",
        "    random_state=42,     # Reproducibility\n",
        "    stratify=y           # Keep class proportions balanced in both sets\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "print(f'Training set   : {X_train.shape[0]} rows')\n",
        "print(f'Testing set    : {X_test.shape[0]} rows')"
      ],

      "source": [
        "#  Task 2: Scale Features\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── 2f. Scale / Normalize Numerical Features ────────────────────────────────\n",
        "# Neural networks train much better when all features are on the same scale.\n",
        "# Without scaling, a feature like 'monthly_charges_inr' (range: 255–2156)\n",
        "# would dominate over 'referral_count' (range: 0–7).\n",
        "#\n",
        "# StandardScaler transforms each feature so it has:\n",
        "#   mean = 0 and standard deviation = 1\n",
        "#\n",
        "# IMPORTANT: We fit the scaler ONLY on training data, then apply to both.\n",
        "# Fitting on test data would cause 'data leakage' (cheating).\n",
        "\n",
        "scaler = StandardScaler()\n",
        "\n",
        "X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)   # Learn the scale from training data\n",
        "X_test_scaled  = scaler.transform(X_test)        # Apply the same scale to test data\n",
        "\n",
        "print('Scaling complete.')\n",
        "print(f'Training feature mean (should be ~0): {X_train_scaled.mean():.4f}')\n",
        "print(f'Training feature std  (should be ~1): {X_train_scaled.std():.4f}')"
      ],
      "metadata": {

      "source": [
        "#  Task 3: Build the Model\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Helper function to build the neural network ──────────────────────────────\n",
        "def build_model(input_dim,\n",
        "                hidden_units=[32, 16],\n",
        "                activation='relu',\n",
        "                learning_rate=0.001):\n",
        "    \"\"\"\n",
        "    Builds a feed-forward neural network for binary classification.\n",
        "\n",
        "    Parameters:\n",
        "    -----------\n",
        "    input_dim     : Number of input features (columns in X)\n",
        "    hidden_units  : List of neuron counts per hidden layer\n",
        "    activation    : Activation function for hidden layers\n",
        "    learning_rate : How fast the model updates its weights during training\n",
        "    \"\"\"\n",
        "\n",
        "    model = keras.Sequential()  # Sequential = layers stacked one after another\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── INPUT LAYER ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    model.add(layers.Input(shape=(input_dim,)))\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── HIDDEN LAYERS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    # Each hidden layer learns patterns in the data.\n",
        "    # Dropout randomly turns off 20% of neurons to reduce overfitting.\n",
        "    for units in hidden_units:\n",
        "        model.add(layers.Dense(units, activation=activation))\n",
        "        model.add(layers.Dropout(0.2))\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── OUTPUT LAYER ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    # 1 neuron with sigmoid: outputs a probability between 0 and 1\n",
        "    # > 0.5 → predicted churn (1), ≤ 0.5 → predicted retained (0)\n",
        "    model.add(layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid'))\n",
        "\n",
        "    # ── COMPILE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "    model.compile(\n",
        "        optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=learning_rate),\n",
        "        loss='binary_crossentropy',   # Standard loss for binary classification\n",
        "        metrics=['accuracy']\n",
        "    )\n",
        "\n",
        "    return model\n",
        "\n",
        "\n",
        "# Build the baseline model\n",
        "input_dim = X_train_scaled.shape[1]\n",
        "model = build_model(input_dim=input_dim)\n",
        "model.summary()"
      ],

    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "#  Task 4: Train the Model\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Train the model ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "# Compute class weights to handle the imbalance (very few churned customers)\n",
        "# This tells the model: \"pay extra attention to churned customers\"\n",
        "n_samples  = len(y_train)\n",
        "n_churn    = y_train.sum()\n",
        "n_retained = n_samples - n_churn\n",
        "weight_for_0 = n_samples / (2 * n_retained)\n",
        "weight_for_1 = n_samples / (2 * n_churn)\n",
        "class_weights = {0: weight_for_0, 1: weight_for_1}\n",

        "    epochs=50,\n",
        "    batch_size=32,\n",
        "    validation_split=0.2,    # 20% of training data used to monitor during training\n",
        "    class_weight=class_weights,\n",
        "    verbose=1\n",
        ")"

        "#  Task 4: Plot Training Curves\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Plot Training vs Validation Loss and Accuracy ───────────────────────────\n",
        "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4))\n",

        "\n",
        "# Accuracy curves\n",

        "#  Task 4: Evaluate on Test Set\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Evaluate on Test Set ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "train_loss, train_acc = model.evaluate(X_train_scaled, y_train, verbose=0)\n",
        "test_loss,  test_acc  = model.evaluate(X_test_scaled,  y_test,  verbose=0)\n",
        "\n",
        "print('=== Model Performance ===')\n",
        "print(f'Training Accuracy : {train_acc*100:.2f}%  |  Training Loss : {train_loss:.4f}')\n",
        "print(f'Testing  Accuracy : {test_acc*100:.2f}%  |  Testing  Loss : {test_loss:.4f}')"
      ],

    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "# Task 4: Confusion Matrix\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Confusion Matrix and Classification Report ───────────────────────────────\n",
        "# Probabilities > 0.5 → predicted churn (1), else retained (0)\n",
        "y_pred_prob = model.predict(X_test_scaled, verbose=0)\n",
        "y_pred = (y_pred_prob > 0.5).astype(int).flatten()\n",
        "\n",
        "cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)\n",
        "\n",
        "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))\n",
        "\n",
        "# Confusion matrix plot\n",
        "disp = ConfusionMatrixDisplay(confusion_matrix=cm,\n",
        "                               display_labels=['Retained (0)', 'Churned (1)'])\n",
        "disp.plot(ax=axes[0], colorbar=False, cmap='Blues')\n",
        "axes[0].set_title('Confusion Matrix', fontsize=13)\n",
        "\n",
        "# Prediction probability distribution\n",
        "axes[1].hist(y_pred_prob, bins=30, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black')\n",
        "axes[1].axvline(0.5, color='red', linestyle='--', label='Decision boundary (0.5)')\n",
        "axes[1].set_title('Distribution of Predicted Probabilities')\n",
        "axes[1].set_xlabel('Predicted Churn Probability')\n",
        "axes[1].set_ylabel('Count')\n",
        "axes[1].legend()\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.suptitle('Task 4: Evaluation Outputs', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')\n",
        "plt.tight_layout()\n",
        "plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "print('=== Classification Report ===')\n",
        "print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=['Retained (0)', 'Churned (1)']))"
      ],

    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "#  Task 5: Hyperparameter Experiments\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Define and Run 4 Experiments ────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "experiments = [\n",
        "    {\n",
        "        'name': 'Baseline',\n",
        "        'hidden_units': [32, 16], 'activation': 'relu',\n",
        "        'learning_rate': 0.001, 'batch_size': 32, 'epochs': 50,\n",
        "        'description': 'Default configuration'\n",
        "    },\n",
        "    {\n",
        "        'name': 'Deeper Network',\n",
        "        'hidden_units': [64, 32, 16], 'activation': 'relu',\n",
        "        'learning_rate': 0.001, 'batch_size': 32, 'epochs': 50,\n",
        "        'description': 'Added one more hidden layer with 64 neurons'\n",
        "    },\n",
        "    {\n",
        "        'name': 'High Learning Rate',\n",
        "        'hidden_units': [32, 16], 'activation': 'relu',\n",
        "        'learning_rate': 0.01, 'batch_size': 32, 'epochs': 50,\n",
        "        'description': 'Increased learning rate from 0.001 to 0.01'\n",
        "    },\n",
        "    {\n",
        "        'name': 'Tanh + Larger Batch',\n",
        "        'hidden_units': [32, 16], 'activation': 'tanh',\n",
        "        'learning_rate': 0.001, 'batch_size': 64, 'epochs': 50,\n",
        "        'description': 'Changed activation to tanh, batch size to 64'\n",
        "    }\n",
        "]\n",
        "\n",
        "results = []\n",
        "\n",
        "for exp in experiments:\n",
        "    print(f\"\\n{'='*50}\")\n",
        "    print(f\"Running: {exp['name']} — {exp['description']}\")\n",
        "    print(f\"{'='*50}\")\n",
        "\n",
        "    m = build_model(\n",
        "        input_dim=input_dim,\n",
        "        hidden_units=exp['hidden_units'],\n",
        "        activation=exp['activation'],\n",
        "        learning_rate=exp['learning_rate']\n",
        "    )\n",
        "\n",
        "    m.fit(\n",
        "        X_train_scaled, y_train,\n",
        "        epochs=exp['epochs'],\n",
        "        batch_size=exp['batch_size'],\n",
        "        validation_split=0.2,\n",
        "        class_weight=class_weights,\n",
        "        verbose=0\n",
        "    )\n",
        "\n",
        "    tr_loss, tr_acc = m.evaluate(X_train_scaled, y_train, verbose=0)\n",
        "    ts_loss, ts_acc = m.evaluate(X_test_scaled,  y_test,  verbose=0)\n",
        "\n",
        "    results.append({\n",
        "        'Configuration'     : exp['name'],\n",
        "        'Hidden Layers'     : str(exp['hidden_units']),\n",
        "        'Activation'        : exp['activation'],\n",
        "        'Learning Rate'     : exp['learning_rate'],\n",
        "        'Batch Size'        : exp['batch_size'],\n",
        "        'Train Accuracy (%)': round(tr_acc * 100, 2),\n",
        "        'Test Accuracy (%)' : round(ts_acc * 100, 2),\n",
        "        'Test Loss'         : round(ts_loss, 4),\n",
        "    })\n",
        "\n",
        "    print(f\"  Train Acc: {tr_acc*100:.2f}% | Test Acc: {ts_acc*100:.2f}% | Test Loss: {ts_loss:.4f}\")\n",
        "\n",
        "print('\\n✓ All experiments complete!')"
      ],

      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "# Task 6: Final Reflection\n",
        "\n",
        "# ─── Final Reflection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n",
        "print(\"\"\"\n",
        "1. WEIGHTS AND BIASES\n",
        "   Weights decide how much importance each input feature gets.\n",
        "   Biases allow the model to shift its output regardless of input.\n",
        "   Both are learned automatically during training via backpropagation.\n",
        "\n",
        "2. WHY ACTIVATION FUNCTIONS ARE NEEDED\n",
        "   Without them, stacking many layers is still just a straight line (linear).\n",
        "   ReLU and tanh introduce curves so the model can learn complex patterns.\n",
        "\n",
        "3. LEARNING RATE — TOO HIGH vs TOO LOW\n",
        "   Too high (e.g. 0.1)   → model overshoots, training becomes unstable\n",
        "   Too low  (e.g. 0.00001) → model learns too slowly, may never converge\n",
        "   Just right (0.001 with Adam) → stable, gradual improvement each epoch\n",
        "\n",
        "4. OVERFITTING vs UNDERFITTING\n",
        "   Overfitting  : Training accuracy >> Test accuracy (memorized training data)\n",
        "   Underfitting : Both accuracies are low (model too simple to learn patterns)\n",
        "   Our model uses Dropout and class_weight to reduce overfitting.\n",
        "   The extreme imbalance (1.5% churn) makes recall on churned class the key metric.\n",
        "\"\"\")"
      ],
